messages:
Carla R: quick question—we currently ship both an OCI-layout bundle and a gzipped tar for onprem installs. operators are confused about which to use for airgapped sites. does anyone have a concise recommendation for compatibility vs operator UX?

Dave M: my take: converge on a single canonical on-disk index (content-addressed JSON manifest) and allow 2 transport formats (OCI layout + tarball) that both contain the same index. that way verifiers only need to check the index + sig. keeps runtime simple.

Alice K: +1 on single canonical index. important for delta updates: index should list chunk ids and byte ranges so delta apply can be deterministic. also makes resume/retry easier for flaky transfer media.

Ben T: concern: some regulated customers ban any OCI tooling. they require a single-file artifact that can be checksumed easily and handed to security. tarball is easier for them. how do we not break UX for those folks?

Dave M: suggestion: provide an opt-in "tar-friendly" packaging mode that embeds the canonical index at /redwood/index.json and includes an additional metadata file /redwood/activation.json. operator CLI then has two fast paths:
```
# verify tar bundle
redwood-pkg verify --file redwood-bundle.tar.gz --key /etc/redwood/pub.pem
# verify OCI layout (registry or fs)
redwood-pkg verify --oci /path/to/oci-layout --key /etc/redwood/pub.pem
```
Both just validate the index + detached signature.

ops-sam: from ops POV: the CLI must clearly print whether this is a full bundle or a delta and whether rollbacks are possible. also show activation window and whether activation requires node quiesce. currently the tar path hides these details.

Carla R: can we add a tiny manifest field like "activation_hints" with values: [requires_quiesce, supports_rollback, delta_compatible]? that would let UI/offline checklist show the right prompts.

Ben T: security asks that signatures be detached and hardware-backed where possible. let's store a per-bundle signature (detached) and allow a KMS/HSM URI in activation.json. admins can provide local public keys for verification.

Dave M: agree. I propose the RFC follow-up: define v1 index schema + detached signature scheme + minimal CLI UX. also define rollback contract (what it means for a component to be "rollback-safe"). I'll draft. owner: me.

Alice K: small nit: for delta generation, index must record original bundle id + base snapshot id (content-addressed). otherwise you can't verify provenance of a delta.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: note: pkg-verifier v0.7.0 was released to staging with content-addressed index support.

ops-sam: one more ops edge: airgapped TLS cert rotation. when we recommend registry-based OCI layout on an isolated registry, we need documented steps for rotating certs used by the registry and for seeding trust on nodes. otherwise upgrades will mysteriously fail after cert expiry.

Dave M: good call. add cert rotation checklist to the RFC and a recommended minimal local CA workflow for customers using OCI layout in airgap mode.

Carla R: thanks all—this helps. can we include a short "operator decision tree" in the RFC: "if security policy forbids registries -> tar-only + detached-signatures; else -> OCI layout preferred for incremental/delta efficiency". that keeps recommendations prescriptive. :thumbsup:

Ben T: :eyes: also consider a tiny compatibility shim in the bootstrapper that accepts both formats and normalizes them into the canonical index dir before verify/apply. simplifies long-term support.

Dave M: noted. I'll include a small sketch of the shim and sample CLI invocations in the RFC. planning to circulate a first draft by EOD Friday. feedback welcome. :shipit:

Carla R: awesome — please @channel when the draft is up.

infra-bot: audit-log: thread updated by Dave M
